correctness.rationale: The scale-two graph Čech complex is the union of full closed-neighborhood simplices Δ(S_u∪S_v) indexed by original edges e=uv. In a triangle-free H the line-graph clique complex is Y=∪_v Δ(S_v). Any face of K outside Y contains two disjoint original edges, and girth≥5 ensures precisely one connecting original edge e that could generate a containing closed neighborhood; two connectors would make a triangle or four-cycle. Pair every lower exterior face σ not containing e with σ∪{e}, and remove pairs in descending cardinality of lower faces; any other exterior coface has an already-removed larger lower partner, so each is a genuine free-face collapse. Thus K collapses simplicially to Y. The star-simplex nerve equals H because pairwise intersections are singleton original edges and triple intersections are empty, giving homotopy wedge of |E|-|V|+1 circles. The H1 map from L(H) is onto; its kernel consists of independent clique-cycle lattices per original vertex, rank Σ_v binom(deg(v)-1,2). The C3/C4 examples demonstrate both exclusion hypotheses are necessary for an unrestricted statement. The inspected finite verifier checks face partitions and explicit freeness on several graphs, but the general proof is combinatorial.
